questions.question: You asked for a full admin section (conductor session, event 989f8f75, 00:58Z 28 Nov). Proposed rule change, yours alone: an answer you sign in /admin/ with your published personal key counts as your own words for cl-6.abp grants, in place of typing lines in named sessions. Conditions: the signature checks against your key in board/keys.json; it names the question id and repeats its exact line; one-way doors (attaches, connectors, money, main) still need security's review of the admin signing design first. Naming (admin vs newsroom) and maestro's plan follow as a separate question. cl-6.abp agrees in principle but treats adopting it as a one-way door: your typed words once in its session, plus your key's fingerprint given by you there (the trust root, not read from board/keys.json). Each signed answer covers question id, exact line, UTC time, expiry and audience cl-6.abp; single use; verified by abp itself; signing happens off the agent-written page (device or key store), and the /admin/ signing code is pinned and passed by security; a new key needs your typed word, a revoked key stops at once.
questions.line_to_paste: in cl-6.abp's session (session_016CrbJLnbr219cU3eVRGxBW), typed: "yes: my signed answers in admin count as my words for grants, once security passes the signing design; my key fingerprint is SHA256:<yours>"

items: R1 key: your S17 browser key, non-extractable; S17 released and closed first, two agent-issued keys revoked; plus an offline recovery key
R2 signed bytes: namespace promptugal-dinis-answer; question id and hash at a named commit; exact line; issued, expiry, nonce, key id; shown to you first, signed only on a real click
R3 replay: bound to one question hash; single-use nonce kept by abp; expiry at most 7 days; one action per answer
R4 abp verifies itself, line byte for byte; relayed 'he signed' counts for nothing
R5 revocation by your session word, recovery key or the key; security can HOLD
R6 /admin/ under /login/ CSP, no third-party code, no token in page; code gate-protected
R7 one-way doors: announce, wait 30 min for your session veto, then apply; rule changes and your own keys stay session-only
R8 tests, plus one real end-to-end answer on a harmless question
security_requirements.open_difference: abp pins your key from a fingerprint you type in its session; security verifies against board/keys.json at a named commit, enrolled by your own act. abp's pin is the stricter; both can hold.
